description: tRIBS is the TIN-based Real-Time Integrated Basin Simulator, a continuous distributed hydrological model released by the tRIBS Model developers. It represents infiltration, soil and groundwater interactions, vegetation, snow and flow routing on a triangulated irregular network. Meteorological forcing and soil or vegetation information can come from station tables or raster products. Outputs include basin discharge, hydrological time series and spatial fields. The model supports water-supply and flood studies, including channel transmission losses and reservoir routing. Geographic coverage and simulation period are user-defined, and mesh detail can vary across the watershed. GitHub provides the C++ source free under MIT, with serial and parallel execution documented. A limitation is the need to prepare and check a consistent mesh, forcing and parameter set before use. The JOSS paper describes version 5.2; the current manual documents version 6.0, so reproducibility requires selecting a release. No directly related catalogue record was established. The model and benchmark data were not downloaded or executed.
